page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores clocked at up to 3.9 GHz, backed by an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). The hardware allocation pairs these computational resources with 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 950 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 17 Gbps baseline network capability.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive throughput across memory and compute tasks. Single-core performance registers in the top tier on Geekbench (2233.0) and delivers strong results in compression workloads, achieving 34.27 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Text processing and small model LLM text generation (355.73 tokens/sec) also place in the upper performance percentiles. Across multi-core benchmarks, the instance yields average tier results, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 13764.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 29292.74, while memory bandwidth achieves 118.04 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 67.72 GB/sec for writes.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the r8idb.4xlarge reflects its high memory density and integrated local NVMe storage. Systems requiring rapid temporary scratch space or low-latency disk caching benefit from bundled high-speed instance storage without incurring external block storage overhead. The configuration is primarily suited for memory-bound relational and in-memory databases such as Redis, large-scale caching layers, real-time data analytics, and intermediate ETL staging.

The processor features hardware acceleration for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core Geekbench and text processing execution alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression throughput. The hardware configuration is specifically targeted at memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory datastores, distributed caching layers, relational databases requiring fast scratch storage, and data processing pipelines.
